diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, among  affine transports, the EnKU is near-optimal for exact distributional conditioning beyond the Gaussian setting.

If we drop this and allow \emph{fully $y_\star$–dependent} affine maps $L_{y_\star}(x,y)=A(y_\star)x+B(y_\star)y+c(y_\star)$, the situation changes: one can engineer many non-Gaussian $\pi$ with exact affine transports that lie strictly beyond $\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims F characterizes the maximal exact set achievable by any affine conditioning map ('any measure-dependent affine transport' and 'among affine transports'). But F is defined as the union of exact sets over weakly y*-dependent maps only (those with A(π) and B(π) independent of y*). The paper's own Section 3.2 gives explicit counterexamples—such as the scaled-pushforward construction and the rotated hypercube—where fully y*-dependent affine maps achieve exactness strictly beyond E^EnKU and hence beyond F. The optimality claim is therefore valid only within the restricted class of weakly y*-dependent maps.

failure_location.quote: we ask what the largest possible set of measures  $\mathrm{F}$ is that any measure-dependent affine transport could be exact for

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'any measure-dependent affine transport' with 'any weakly y*-dependent affine transport' and 'among affine transports' with 'among weakly y*-dependent affine transports' in the abstract. The formal results already correctly scope to weakly y*-dependent maps.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract materially misleads readers about the scope of the maximality result Theorem thm:F_char. The near-optimality of the EnKU holds only among weakly y*-dependent affine conditioning maps, not among all affine conditioning maps as advertised.
issues.title: Abstract overstates scope of F as maximal exact set among all affine transports
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local wording correction in the abstract that aligns the prose with the already-correct formal statements. Every substantive claim and guarantee survives; only the overstated scope is corrected, with no new argument needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims the EnKU is the unique exact affine update for any measure in F except a symmetric subclass. But Theorem thm:F_char shows F = E^EnKU ∪ S_nl-dec, and for measures in S_nl-dec \ E^EnKU the EnKU is not exact at all—these measures have exact affine updates only through other weakly y*-dependent maps. The uniqueness result Corollary cor:enkf_char applies only to measures in E^EnKU \ (S_cov ∪ S_dec ∪ S_cyc), which is a strict subset of F. Measures in S_nl-dec \ E^EnKU are not merely 'strongly symmetric distributions' where the EnKU is non-unique; they are measures where the EnKU fails to be exact entirely.

failure_location.quote: Further, it is the unique affine update achieving exact conditioning for any measure in $\mathrm{F}$ except for a subclass of strongly symmetric distributions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change 'for any measure in F' to 'for any measure in E^EnKU' in the abstract's uniqueness claim, matching the scope of Corollary cor:enkf_char. The exception class 'strongly symmetric distributions' already covers S_cov ∪ S_dec ∪ S_cyc.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract overstates the uniqueness guarantee by a full quantifier: it claims uniqueness on F when the result holds only on E^EnKU minus three symmetry classes. Readers may incorrectly believe the EnKU achieves exact conditioning on all of F and is unique there.
issues.title: Abstract claims EnKU uniqueness for all measures in F, including measures where EnKU is not exact
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single quantifier correction (F to E^EnKU) in the abstract. All formal results are correctly stated and proved; only the abstract's restatement overreaches. The conclusion and guarantees of Corollary cor:enkf_char survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This is a simple consequence of the fact that $X + BY$ is Gaussian and there is an affine transport map between any two non-singular Gaussians.

issues.failure_explanation: The claim asserts that for any matrix B with Cov(X+BY) full rank, there exist A and c making Ax+By+c exact for Gaussian π. Exactness requires Cov(AX+BY) = Σ_{X|Y}. For a 1D standard Gaussian pair with correlation ρ=0.5 (so Σ_{X|Y}=0.75), choosing B=2 satisfies Cov(X+2Y)=7>0 but Cov(AX+2Y)=A²+2A+4=(A+1)²+3≥3>0.75 for all real A; the discriminant of A²+2A+3.25=0 is −9<0. The underlying reasoning error is conflating the existence of an affine map between X+BY and X|Y=y* (true for full-rank Gaussians) with the existence of such a map whose y-coefficient equals the prescribed B: the Brenier-type map from X+BY to X|Y=y* has y-coefficient A′B, not B, unless A′B = B.

failure_location.quote: for every choice of $B$ (assuming $\Cov(X+BY)$ has full rank for all $y_\star$) there are $A$  and $c$ such that $L_{\pi,y_\star}(x,y)= A(\pi,y_\star)x + B(\pi,y_\star)y + c(\pi,y_\star)$ is exact.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the claim to state that infinitely many affine conditioning maps (without 'for every choice of B') are exact for Gaussian joints, or restrict B to a neighborhood of −K where the covariance-matching equation AGAᵀ+(AK+B)Σ_YY(AK+B)ᵀ=G is solvable in A. Both fixes preserve the motivational point about non-uniqueness.
issues.overall_effect: The introduction overstates the degree of freedom in choosing exact affine maps for Gaussian joints. Non-uniqueness of exact affine maps for Gaussians remains true (e.g., for B = −K any orthogonal A works), but not for every B as claimed. No formal result depends on this assertion.
issues.title: Introduction falsely claims exactness for every choice of B for Gaussian joints
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local weakening or restriction of an illustrative example in the introduction. The non-uniqueness motivating the paper is preserved, no formal result depends on the claim, and no new argument is needed to state the corrected version.
